thread:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a focused autotune job on A100 for the transformer kernel. changed tile / smem layout and register allocation hints. short summary: smaller tile (32) + warp-specialize path gave ~8% p50 improvement for seq=256, but regression for seq>=1024 (~+12% latency).

kevin: can you paste the kernel launch + smem numbers? wondering about dynamic smem vs per-block.

alex: sure — here's the launch we used: 
```
// kernel config
dim3 grid = {1024};
dim3 block = {256};
size_t dynamic_smem = 48*1024; // bytes
transformer_kernel<<<grid, block, dynamic_smem>>>(...);
```
profiling snapshot from perf-bot: 
```
perf-bot: kernel=transformer_tile32_warpSpec, SM_occupancy=0.42, registers_per_thread=56, used_smem=46KB, achieved_occupancy=0.65, L2_bw=120GB/s
```

maria: interesting. registers are a bit high for block=256 — that could explain lower occupancy on long sequences where KV cache grows and we see spill behavior. did you try block=128?

alex: yes — block=128 + same tile dropped regs/thread to 48 and bumped SM occupancy to 0.58; latency for seq=1024 improved vs block=256 but still slightly worse than baseline. baseline is tile=64, block=256, reg=40.

kevin: baseline reg=40? how did reg change so much with tile size? is the compiler unrolling or doing different vec loads for tile=32?

alex: compiler emits a narrower dot-product loop for tile=32 which introduced more local temps for tiling, hence reg pressure. also we enabled #pragma unroll(4) in one variant which made it worse.

sarah: two angles: 1) try lowering unroll or use pragma maybe conditional on seq_len; 2) move some temp buffers to shared if that helps reduce reg usage but watch smem capacity.

maria: regarding KV cache: when seq grows, per-thread KV pointers increase, that can blow working set and cause more register spills to local memory — which kills perf. Did you capture memory stall counters?

alex: yep — perf-bot output shows local_load_store_stalls up ~30% on seq=2048 for tile=32 variant. L1 hit-rate dropped from 82%->66%.

perf-bot: autotune run summary attached: variants tested = [tile64_blk256, tile32_blk256, tile32_blk128, tile48_blk192]; best for seq<=512 = tile32_blk128; best for seq>=1024 = tile64_blk256. global best compromise = tile48_blk192 (avg p95 +3% but stable).

kevin: alright — seems like we need a sequence-length-aware kernel pick in the runtime. pick tile32 path for short queries and tile64 for long ones. can we make the fallback automatic in kernel selector?

maria: yes — we can add a lightweight heuristic: if requested max_seq <= 512 use warp-specialized tile32 path; else use conservative tile64 path. also consider realtime switching when KV cache size grows beyond threshold.

alex: one catch: switching kernels implies different binary variants and smem footprints. launching the other kernel sometimes changes overall scheduler decisions (SM allocation) and causes short-lived tail spikes. we saw a 200ms tail bump during canary.

sarah: maybe implement a gradual rollout: route small fraction of traffic to new kernel and measure P99. Also expose a per-customer override in Dedicated to pin path.

kevin: agree. also we should add fallback policy: if L1 miss rate > 25% or local_store_stalls > 20% for 30s, fallback to tile64. that keeps latency SLO.

maria: I'll add the heuristic + telemetry + fallback to the selector PR. tagging @alex for kernel launch tuning tests and @sarah for rollout plan.

alex: cool — I'll upload micro-benchmarks and the perf traces to the ticket: infra/eng-runtime#789. quick paste of a micro result: seq=256 p50: baseline 12.8ms -> tile32_blk128 11.7ms, seq=2048 p50 baseline 68.2ms -> tile64_blk256 62.5ms.

kevin: thanks. next steps: (1) land selector heuristic, (2) build canary with traffic split 5%, (3) watch perf-bot counters, (4) if tail spikes -> rollback. :hammer_and_wrench: :eyes:

perf-bot: scheduled autotune job 1775008901 queued (will run full sweep on T4/A100).
